title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative:
In 2022, the African Union Commission (AUC) adopted continental guidelines on Bilateral Labour Agreements (BLAs) to serve as a guide to support Member States in strengthening protection mechanisms for migrant workers through international cooperation.
The African Union (AU) also adopted a Declaration on the Protection and Promotion of the Rights of Migrant Workers. The drafting of the AU Declaration followed an inclusive and participatory process and included Member States, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), Pan African Parliament and the tripartite AU Labour Migration Advisory Committee (LMAC). Both documents have been endorsed at the fourth AU Specialised Technical Committee on Social Development, Labour and Employment (STC-SDLE) meeting held in April 2022.
Both documents took into account perspectives of constituents through a participatory consultative process; and draw from international labour standards, the UN guidance on development of Bilateral Labour Migration Agreements among others.
The systematic regular review process of the progress made in implementing the provisions of the Declaration and the guidelines is done under the STC monitoring framework.
In 2023, the knowledge sharing platform prototype on skills and labour migration has been integrated into the African Skills Portal for Youth Employment and Entrepreneurship portal hosted by the African Union Development Agency - New Partnership for African Development (AUDA-NEPAD). The portal is a continental knowledge sharing platform that enables practitioners and policymakers across the African continent to share, collaborate and engage with each other. The platform caters for exchange of knowledge, good practices and policy approaches within the continent on issues related to skills and labour migration. The ILO, with support from the Government of Sweden:
- Developed a draft of the African Union guidelines on Bilateral Labour Agreements (BLAs) and the Declaration on the protection and promotion of the rights of migrant workers.
- Organized technical consultations with workers' and employers’ organisations at regional level and consolidated technical inputs from ILO staff and stakeholders. For the Declaration, for example, a survey tailored to worker and employer organizations was distributed through the ILO.
- ILO’s instruments (tools, publications and Labour standards) were extensively used to draft the Declaration (Annex 1 of the AU Declaration report) and the AU BLA model.
- The ILO helped organize the fourth Ordinary Session of the Specialized Technical Committee (STC) on Social Development, Labour and Employment that led to the endorsement of the Declaration and Guidelines.
Implementation of the Declaration and the Guidelines is part of the ILO-AUC Joint implementation Programme (JOP) renewed in 2022.
With the support of the United Kingdom's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, the ILO developed a knowledge sharing platform prototype on skills and labour migration in 2022. In 2023, the ILO operationalized the prototype and integrated it into the African Union Development Agency - New Partnership for African Development (AUDA-NEPAD) hosted portal called African Skills Portal for Youth Employment and Entrepreneurship.
